about.historySubtitle: Our spiritual journey through the decades
about.historyP1: Holy Virgin Mary Russian Orthodox Cathedral is a parish of the Diocese of San Francisco and the West, Orthodox Church in America (OCA), which received its autocephaly from the Russian Orthodox Church in 1971. The Cathedral is dedicated to the icon of the Holy Virgin Mary "Rescue of the Perishing" with its yearly Parish Feast celebrated on February 5th or the closest Sunday.
about.historyP2: The parish was founded by tsarist Russia's emigres in 1923, making it the first Russian parish in Southern California. In 1928 Metropolitan Platon and Bishop Alexei consecrated this temple to continuously attend to the spiritual needs of Russian immigrants, and starting in the 1960s, to the American population seeking salvation within the Orthodox Church.
about.historyP3: The Cathedral is built according to the 14th century Pskov Orthodox architectural tradition which does not assume the presence of any musical instruments or pews. The faithful gather here to worship and glorify the Lord; therefore any immodest or inappropriate attire, ill-mannered conduct, ringing cell phones and conversations are unacceptable during the services.
about.historyP4: Every year Holy Virgin Mary Cathedral organizes various events and fund-raising luncheons. Next to our main Parish Feast marked by the arrival of our ruling Bishop, the parish hosts a Slavic Festival of food, culture and folklore every second Sunday of November. In December there is a Christmas Bazaar with the sale of homemade baked goods. The parish invites everyone to the following fund-raisers: Blini (Maslenitsa) Luncheon, Christmas Eve dinner, Verba bouquet and Koulich sale (Lazarus Saturday), Paschal meal, and more. We welcome you to join us!

ministries.xeniaDesc: The St. Ksenia Society is a parish organization which provides assistance to homeless people in — but not limited to — the surrounding Silver Lake area. They deliver meals, clothing, and items of personal hygiene to those experiencing homelessness and those in need. It organizes charitable projects for the benefit of the homeless in Silver Lake by collecting funds, sponsoring meals, and other enterprises.
ministries.xeniaA1: Meal delivery to homeless individuals in the Silver Lake area
ministries.xeniaA2: Clothing and personal hygiene item distribution
ministries.xeniaA4: Fund-raising events and sponsoring communal meals
ministries.xeniaA5: Outreach to those in need in and around Silver Lake
ministries.donateText: Your donations directly fund outreach materials, food, clothing, and transportation for our volunteers.
ministries.choirDesc: The Festal Choir at Holy Virgin Mary Russian Orthodox Cathedral is composed of men and women who dedicate their time to learning the tradition of singing in the Orthodox Church. Singing for an extensive schedule of services, the choir brings voice to the corporal prayer of the assembled faithful throughout the liturgical year.
ministries.choirAboutText: Under the direction of Reader Serge Liberovsky, singers gather for regular rehearsals to hone their singing skills and prepare liturgical texts for services. While the choir is mixed (comprised of both men and women), the repertoire draws heavily on the monastic traditions of the Trinity-St. Sergius and Kyiv-Caves Lavras, with singers joining their voices in both English and Church Slavonic.
ministries.rehearsalSchedule: Regular rehearsals are held in the parish hall. New singers are always welcome. Please speak with Reader Serge following any service for more information.
ministries.joinChoirText: Those interested in singing and joining the choir should speak with Reader Serge following any service. With the blessing of the rector, all new singers will take an informal audition to assess their musical abilities and voice placement.
ministries.catDesc: The Catechism School offers systematic instruction in the Orthodox Christian faith for adults and older youth. Whether you are preparing for reception into the Church, deepening your knowledge, or exploring Orthodoxy for the first time, you are welcome here.
ministries.catScheduleText: Classes are held on Sunday mornings from 9:00 AM to 10:00 AM, before the Divine Liturgy. Additional evening sessions are offered on the first Wednesday of each month at 7:00 PM.
ministries.catContactText: To enroll or for more information, please contact the parish office or speak with the rector after services.
ministries.sisterDesc: The Sisterhood of the Holy Virgin Mary Church Cathedral takes care of the decoration of the Church, the vestments and the furnishing of the parish buildings and garden, and finances charitable works by collecting funds, sponsoring luncheons and other enterprises.
ministries.sisterM1: Care of church decoration, vestments, and furnishings
ministries.sisterM3: Organization of parish lunches and fund-raising luncheons
ministries.sisterM4: Charitable fund-raising and sponsoring parish enterprises
ministries.sisterM5: Support of Orthodox theological seminaries and the Diocese of the West
ministries.sisterJoinText: The Sisterhood welcomes new members and helpers! The Sisterhood is under the protection of the Holy and Lifegiving Trinity and celebrates its Feast Day annually on the 2nd day of Pentecost (Holy Spirit Day). Please speak with the Sisterhood for more information.
ministries.barbaraDesc: In September 2025, with the blessing of Archpriest Nazariy, the Little Sisterhood of Saint Barbara the Great Martyr resumed its activities. Its members—girls aged 5 and older—perform their small church duties during Sunday and feast-day Divine Liturgies. They help care for the candlesticks, distribute prayer sheets to parishioners for communal prayer, collect donations, and perform other duties in the church. By helping and participating in parish life, the girls learn responsibility and a love for the church and its services. The Sisterhood helps them feel like part of the parish family, be of service to their parish, and find their place in the life of the Church.
ministries.lovesDesc: The Los Angeles Orthodox Visitors to Elderly and Sick (L.O.V.E.S.) is a parish organization that visits the elderly and sick in homes, hospitals, and convalescent homes. L.O.V.E.S. provides assistance to parishioners as needed, delivers meals to those unable to attend church, and contributes physical and financial support to St. John of Kronstadt Home for the Elderly.
ministries.lovesA1: Visits to the elderly and sick in homes, hospitals, and convalescent homes
ministries.lovesA3: Meal delivery to those unable to attend church
ministries.lovesA4: Physical and financial support of St. John of Kronstadt Home for the Elderly

services.scheduleSubtitle: All are welcome to join us in worship
services.holyDaysText: Special services are held for all Great Feasts of the Orthodox calendar. Please check the announcements for feast-day service times.
services.weekdayText: Moleben, Panikhida, Akathists, and other services by request. Please contact the church office to schedule.
services.liveDesc: Watch our services live on YouTube. All Sunday Liturgies and major feast day services are broadcast live.
services.noStream: No live stream is currently active. Please check back during service times.
services.archiveDesc: Watch past services and events from our YouTube channel archive.
services.aboutP1: The Divine Liturgy of the Russian Orthodox Church is celebrated according to the ancient Byzantine rite, in Church Slavonic with portions in English. Our services follow the Julian calendar for the calculation of feast days.
services.aboutP2: Visitors and non-Orthodox guests are welcome to attend all services. Please arrive a few minutes early to receive a service bulletin. Our parishioners are happy to help orient newcomers.
services.aboutP3: Holy Communion is offered only to Orthodox Christians who have prepared through fasting and confession. Non-Orthodox guests are invited to receive the blessed bread (Antidoron) at the end of the service.

sundaySchool.infoDesc: Our parish school — the Russian Orthodox Parochial School — meets on Sundays throughout the school year, from September to June. We offer classes for children from preschool through middle school. We learn about the Holy Scriptures and our Orthodox faith, history and geography, sing songs, and do lesson-based crafts and activities. Classes are taught in English, and parents are always welcome to sit in.
sundaySchool.c3: History of the Orthodox Church, Russia and the Cossacks
sundaySchool.scheduleText: Classes meet Sundays from 12:00 PM to 3:35 PM during the school year (September – June), departing from the Liturgy after the conclusion of the Eucharist.
sundaySchool.programDesc: Our program follows a curriculum including Russian language, literature, basics of Orthodox Christianity, music, and history of the Orthodox Church, Russia and the Cossacks.
sundaySchool.pg1: Creating a dynamic environment for preserving love and respect for the spiritual heritage of Orthodoxy, Russian language and traditions
sundaySchool.pg2: Establishing a warm Russian-speaking community for communication
sundaySchool.pg3: Participation in joint trips and events
sundaySchool.pg4: Preparing students for a lifelong Orthodox Christian life
sundaySchool.contactText: For enrollment or more information, email youth@hvmla.org, call (323) 661-7000, or text 323-539-6139. Registration is ongoing — children can join at any time!

education.booksDesc: Our parish library contains a wide selection of Orthodox Christian literature, available for loan to parishioners. Topics include theology, lives of saints, prayer, church history, and iconography.
education.b1Desc: A classic of Russian Orthodox spirituality describing the practice of the Jesus Prayer.
education.b2Desc: A comprehensive overview of Orthodox theology, worship, and tradition.
education.b3Desc: The complete 12-volume collection of saints' lives organized by Orthodox calendar.
education.liturgicalDesc: Download or view liturgical texts used in our services, including the Divine Liturgy, Vespers, Matins, and the services of the Hours.
education.prayerDesc: Orthodox Christian prayer rules and devotional texts for personal and family use.
education.pb3: Canon of Repentance to Our Lord Jesus Christ
education.pb4: Prayers Before and After Holy Communion
education.bulletinDesc: The weekly parish bulletin contains service announcements, upcoming events, spiritual readings, and parish news. Bulletins are available in the narthex every Sunday and can be downloaded here.

support.donationsSubtitle: Your generosity sustains our parish ministry
support.donationsP1: Holy Virgin Mary Cathedral relies on the faithful support of parishioners and friends to maintain our beautiful cathedral, support our clergy and staff, and fund our community ministries.
support.donationsP2: All donations are tax-deductible. Our parish is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization.

support.volunteeringSubtitle: Serve your community through the gift of your time
support.volunteeringDesc: There are many ways to serve our parish community. Whether you have a few hours a month or can commit regularly, your help is always welcome and deeply appreciated.
support.v5: Parish events and feast day preparation
support.volunteerSignupText: To express interest in volunteering, please fill out the contact form on our Contact page or speak with the parish administrator after services.

cafe.cafeDesc: After every Sunday Liturgy, the parish community gathers in the fellowship hall for our traditional coffee hour. The Cathedral Cafe serves light refreshments, homemade pastries, and warm drinks in a welcoming atmosphere. All are invited — parishioners, visitors, and newcomers alike.
cafe.cafeHoursText: Sundays after Divine Liturgy, approximately 12:00 PM – 2:00 PM
cafe.specialEventsText: The Cafe operates during all major parish feast days and fundraising events. Check the parish bulletin for details on special menus and themed evenings.
cafe.museumDesc: The Holy Virgin Mary Cathedral Museum preserves and shares the rich history of the Russian Orthodox diaspora in Los Angeles. Our collection includes historical photographs, liturgical artifacts, vestments, and documents spanning nearly a century of parish life.
cafe.e1: The Russian Emigration: Faith in Exile (1920–1950)
cafe.e2: Building a Cathedral: Architecture and Iconography
cafe.e3: A Century of Worship: Liturgical Treasures
cafe.museumHoursText: Open Sundays after Divine Liturgy (12:00 PM – 2:00 PM) and by appointment.
cafe.museumContact: To arrange a group visit or for more information, please contact the parish office.

bylaws.bylawsDesc: The bylaws of Holy Virgin Mary Russian Orthodox Cathedral set forth the governance, membership, and organizational structure of the parish. They were adopted at the parish assembly on January 30, 2022, ratified effective February 6, 2022, and approved by His Eminence Archbishop Benjamin of San Francisco and the West.
